court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Family Court, Gorakhpur - Criminal Case No. 313 of 2017
case_name: Abhimanu Pandey vs State Of U.P. And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Priyanka Pandey (wife) and State of U.P. (government)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Abhimanu Pandey and Smt. Priyanka Pandey got married in 2008. After some time, their relationship became strained due to harassment and additional demand of dowry. The wife filed an application under section 125 Cr.P.C. for her maintenance alleging that the husband has refused to maintain her.

legal_principles.principle: The court should consider all relevant facts and evidence before passing an order.
legal_principles.held: Learned Family Court without considering any fact brought by the revisionist and without considering the material evidence regarding expenses of treatment of his physically challenged son as well as without considering the amount of loan passed impugned order of maintenance of Rs. 19,000/- per month in favour of respondent no. 2.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not pass an order based on surmises and conjectures.
legal_principles.held: Learned Family Court passed the order only on the basis of surmises and conjectures and wrongly and illegally awarded maintenance of Rs. 19,000/- per month in favour of respondent no. 2 from the date of order without considering the financial burden of revisionist.

legal_principles.principle: The court should consider the financial burden of the person affected by an order.
legal_principles.held: Learned Family Court has passed the impugned order without considering the financial burden of revisionist.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not curtail the rights of dependents without considering all relevant facts.
legal_principles.held: Learned Family Court has passed the impugned order which curtails the rights of dependents of the revisionist without discussing any material fact in this regard as well as without considering the emphasis of section 125 (4) Cr.P.C.

outcome.final_order: The revisionist was directed to pay Rs. 19,000/- per month from the date of order to respondent no. 2 as her maintenance on 11th day of each month.
